sources: Ukrzaliznytsia statement + governor Oleksandr Hanzha + mayor Borys Filatov, via Kyiv Independent / Ukrainska Pravda / Reuters via Straits Times / Interfax
fault_line: Civilian rail as a target: deliberate strike on a crowded commuter platform, or collateral of a rail-infrastructure campaign -- and why were passengers still on the platform under a heightened-danger warning?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT - officials' toll; ATTRIBUTED REPORT - weapon/attribution] A Russian jet-powered drone struck a platform at Dnipro main railway station on the morning of Oct 29, where train No. 866 Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia was standing/preparing to depart, killing 13 people and wounding at least 5 (Kyiv Post update: wounded risen to 10, 3 in serious condition incl. an 11-year-old boy). Ukrzaliznytsia: despite a heightened-danger air-raid warning, people were on the platform. Zelenskyy: 'A horrific Russian strike on the railway station in Dnipro... 13 deaths have been confirmed.' No Russian comment retrieved. Context: overnight Oct 28-29 Russia launched 112 drones (40 jet-powered Shaheds); Ukraine Air Force says 97 downed/jammed, hits at 7 locations.
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct declared families: Reuters T1 (via Straits Times carry; registry: wire carries count as the wire's family), Kyiv Independent T2, Ukrainska Pravda T3, Interfax T3. Kyiv Post and RBC-Ukraine are UNDECLARED and do not add families (wounded-10 update is attribution only).
sections.what_disputed: No Russian statement on Dnipro retrieved in-window; 5 vs 10 wounded differs by update time (5 = initial Hanzha count, 10 = later Kyiv Post update) -- report as 13 killed, at least 5 wounded rising to 10 in later updates, never a single fixed wounded figure. Overnight 112-drone figure is a Ukrainian Air Force claim, not independently verified.
sections.why_matters: LEAD candidate: hard counted toll (13 killed) + civilian-train framing + jet-drone weapon, inside the proven Russia-Ukraine strike lane. Lead with the platform, not the overnight drone count.
